name: GameChanger
tagline: Scorekeeping, stats, and live video streaming for youth and amateur sports teams.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The scorekeeping part is honestly not that hard: a pitch-by-pitch state machine, a box score, and season stat rollups are a weekend of careful work. Everything that makes people actually use GameChanger is the part you cannot build alone: grandparents in another state watching the stream, the rest of the team seeing the same live game feed, and schedules and rosters flowing in from the league. Add mobile apps that survive a dead cell signal at a rural field, video ingest and transcoding, and clip generation tied to each at-bat, and the gap stops being a coding problem. You can build yourself a very good private scorebook. You cannot build the audience that was the reason you opened the app.
coreLoopDIY: A local-first tablet scorebook that records pitch-by-pitch play, produces a live box score, and rolls up per-player season stats you can export.
requirements: A tablet or laptop you can keep charged in a dugout
Someone willing to actually score every pitch
whatYouLose: Live video streaming to family who are not at the field
Automatic clip generation tied to individual plays and at-bats
League and organization integrations that push schedules, rosters, and results
Real-time game following for parents and the rest of the team
Native iOS and Android apps that handle bad field connectivity and later sync
moatNotes: Video ingest, transcoding, and delivery for tens of thousands of simultaneous amateur games is a capital problem, not a code problem.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the subscription is not really buying a scorebook, it is buying the fact that everyone else already has the app. The league publishes schedules into it, the coach scores into it, and the family watches from it, so one person opting out for a self-hosted version just means that person is now doing extra work for a smaller audience. The video side is the other half: streaming a game from a field with two bars of service, storing it, and cutting it into per-play clips is infrastructure spend that a personal build cannot fake.
notes: The scorebook is a weekend; the stadium is not. The moat is video infrastructure plus the fact that the whole league, and every relative watching from out of state, is already inside the app.
prompt:
Build a local-first baseball and softball scorekeeping web app. This is a private scorebook for one team, not a streaming or social product.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Vite + React + TypeScript
- Tailwind for styling
- Dexie (IndexedDB) for all storage, no backend, no accounts, no telemetry
- Installable PWA with a service worker so it works fully offline in a dugout
- Vitest for the scoring engine tests

Data model: Team, Player (name, number, positions), Season, Game (opponent, date, home/away, lineup), and an append-only Event log per game. Every scoring action is an event; all derived state is computed from the log so undo is just popping an event.

Scoring engine, keep it pure and tested:
- Pitch-level tracking: ball, strike, foul, swinging vs called strike
- Plate appearance outcomes: 1B, 2B, 3B, HR, BB, HBP, K, sac fly, sac bunt, fielder's choice, error, reached on error
- Outs by position number, double and triple plays
- Base runner state with steals, caught stealing, pickoffs, wild pitch, passed ball, and manual runner advancement
- Innings, half innings, walk-off and run-rule game endings
- Pitch counts per pitcher, substitutions for batters and pitchers

UI, tablet-first and thumb-friendly:
- Big-button live scoring screen with a diamond showing runners and a one-tap undo
- Live box score: line score, batting lines with AB/R/H/RBI/BB/K, pitching lines with IP/H/R/ER/BB/K
- Season stats page per player with AVG, OBP, SLG, OPS, and pitcher ERA and WHIP
- Roster and schedule editors, all entered by hand

In scope: offline scoring, undo, box scores, season rollups, JSON backup export and import, CSV stat export.
Out of scope, do not attempt: video, streaming, accounts, cloud sync, push notifications, league imports, sharing links.

Ship a README with setup, how to run tests, and a short explanation of the event-sourced scoring model. No secrets are needed; if you ever add any, read them from .env.
